title: Weekend building a trade copier across two prop firm ecosystems (ProjectX → Rithmic) — what broke
author: Kooky-Antelope-4262
selftext:
Got tired of managing multiple funded accounts manually, so I spent the weekend building a copier between my Topstep eval and a Lucid account: master fill → mirrored market orders, running on a small Windows VPS. Sharing because none of this was documented anywhere in one place.

**What broke:**

1. **Rithmic rpCode 13 "permission denied" that wasn't about permissions.** Each prop firm has its own Rithmic *system name*. I was connecting to "Rithmic Paper Trading" — Lucid needs their own string. Burned an evening on this; the error tells you nothing.
2. **One session per credential, everywhere.** R|Trader open = copier can't log in. Worse: TopstepX web and the API fight over one session, so opening the browser to place a test trade kicked my copier off — it could never see the trade I just placed. Had to route master orders through the API itself.
3. **Silent symbol mismatch.** ProjectX says `CON.F.US.MNQ.U26`, Rithmic wants `MNQU6`. My conversion "worked" — orders sent, logs said OK, 14ms — but nothing reached the exchange. Lesson: sent ≠ filled. Subscribe to order notifications or your log lies to you.
4. **A checkbox double-fired an order.** One sell became two on Lucid — manual path and copy path both wrote the same trade. Only caught it because per-account position display disagreed. Divergence alerts got built that same night.

**Where it landed:** Topstep→Topstep copies in \~110–180ms; Topstep→Lucid fill-confirmed in \~20ms — Rithmic's binary protocol beats the same-broker REST leg, which surprised me.

**Questions for anyone running copiers across firms:**

* How do you deal with session-takeover on single-connection platforms? I can't watch TopstepX web while the copier runs.
* Anyone found automation policies clearly in writing? Lucid explicitly permits copiers; Topstep prohibits automation on funded. The gap between firms surprised me.
